quiz_title: Quiz 4: Polyglot & General Assessment (Python, SQL & Algorithms)

questions.title: Subarray Sum Equals K (Python / C / C++ / Any)
questions.problem_statement:
Given an integer N, a target integer K on the first line, and N space-separated integers on the second line, print the number of contiguous subarrays whose sum equals K.

### Input Format
Line 1: `N K`
Line 2: `a_1 a_2 ... a_N`

### Output Format
Single integer: count of subarrays summing to K.
questions.grading_rubric: GREEN for O(N) prefix-sum hashmap or clean loop passing all tests. BLUE for creative generator/itertools/accumulator approach. RED for O(N^2) timeout, off-by-one, or hardcoded outputs.

questions.title: Department Second Highest Salary (SQL Query)
questions.problem_statement: Given table `Employees(id INT, name TEXT, department_id INT, salary INT)`, write an SQL query that returns `(department_id, second_highest_salary)` for every department, handling ties via DENSE_RANK or distinct subquery.
questions.grading_rubric: BLUE if uses DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC). GREEN if uses correlated subquery with MAX(salary) < MAX. RED if forgets PARTITION BY / GROUP BY department_id or fails when salaries tie.

questions.title: Algorithm Design & Complexity Justification (Markdown / Text / Code)
questions.problem_statement: Explain how to detect a cycle in a directed graph in O(V + E) time and state the space complexity. You may submit prose (.txt/.md) or code/pseudocode.
questions.grading_rubric: GREEN for standard 3-color DFS (unvisited/visiting/visited) or Kahn's topological sort (indegree queue) with O(V + E) time and O(V) space. BLUE for Tarjan's SCC or iterative DFS state machine analysis. RED if confuses undirected visited check with directed back-edge detection.
